# setup-maf-evals

Scaffold an `<App>.Evals.Tests` MSTest project that measures latency,
token usage, cost, quality, and safety on every change to a .NET
agentic app — and produces the proper Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation
HTML report by default.

## When to Use

- The user asks to "set up evals", "add an evaluation harness", "wire
  up MEAI evaluation", or "measure my agent's quality".
- The user wants to **validate quality** after a model change ("does
  swapping gpt-4o → gpt-4o-mini regress responses?") and needs a
  reproducible baseline.
- The user wants to **compare** model assignments side-by-side
  ("compare gpt-4o vs gpt-4o-mini across my agents").
- The user wants to **add safety evaluators** (Hate/Violence/SelfHarm/
  Sexual via Azure AI Foundry) to an existing agent.
- The user wants a recurring eval run wired into CI (the optional
  GitHub Actions workflow).

## When Not to Use

- The user wants a **one-shot audit** of existing code without scaffolding
  a new test project — use `scan-agentic-app-perf` instead.
- The user wants **always-on perf guard-rails** in the project's
  agent-instructions file — use `configure-agentic-perf-rules`.
- The project is not a .NET agentic app, or the user is not using
  `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` / `Microsoft.Agents.AI`.
- The user explicitly does not want an MSTest dependency and is not
  willing to use the opt-in `--shape console` runner.

## Supported topologies

The skill targets any .NET project using Microsoft Agent Framework
(`Microsoft.Agents.AI`), regardless of how it's hosted:

- **Aspire AppHost** (`*.AppHost.csproj` orchestrating agent services) — the
  most common shape; the generated `AgentChatClientFactory` mirrors the
  AppHost's connection-string-driven `IChatClient` registration.
- **Plain console / worker service** — `Microsoft.Agents.AI` registered
  directly against an OpenAI or Foundry client without an Aspire AppHost.
  The factory mirrors the app's direct registration (e.g. `AddOpenAIClient`
  or `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient` at the host level).
- **ASP.NET Core minimal API** — agents registered via the same DI patterns.

`IChatClient` detection (see `references/ichatclient-detection.md`) works
the same way across all topologies; only the AppHost-vs-Program.cs search
locations differ.

## Workflow

### 1. Discover the target app

Detect:

- Solution file (`*.sln` / `*.slnx`)
- AppHost project name (`*.AppHost.csproj`)
- Agent service projects
- Existing test / eval projects (avoid clobbering)
- **`IChatClient` registration** (scan AppHost + agent projects for
  `AddChatClient` / `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient` / `AddOllamaChatClient`
  / `AddOpenAIChatClient` and any explicit `services.AddSingleton<IChatClient>` or
  Foundry deployment alias references). See `references/ichatclient-detection.md`.

If no agentic app is detected, abort. If a `*.Evals.Tests` project already
exists, switch to update mode (see step 1a).

### 1a. Update mode (when `*.Evals.Tests` project already exists)

File classes:

| Class            | Files                                                                  | Behavior on update         |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| **infra**        | `*.Evals.Tests.csproj`, `dotnet-tools.json`, `Reporting/*`, `Wire/*`, test class skeletons | merge package refs; create file if missing; do **not** overwrite |
| **user data**    | `Quality/rubric.md`, `Quality/golden.json`, `Compare/matrix.json`, `Telemetry/inputs.json`, `Telemetry/prices.json`, `quality.thresholds.json`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml` | never overwrite; create if missing |
| **generated**    | `.copilot/perf-reports/evals/`                                         | regenerate freely          |

If an existing infra file differs from the current template, surface
the diff in the chat output but do not overwrite. Recommend the user
review and merge manually.

`golden.json` has a `schema_version` field. If the detected version is
older than the current template, offer to migrate (additive only —
preserves existing rows, adds the new fields as nullable).

### 2. Confirm scope with the user

Present the detection summary, then confirm:

1. **Project shape** (default: MSTest). Alternative: console runner
   (legacy v1 shape) — only emit if user explicitly asks for it.
2. **Evaluator categories to enable.** Defaults shown; user can override.

   | Category | Evaluators | Cost | Needs | Default |
   |------|-----------|------|-------|---------|
   | **Quality** *(headline)* | Relevance, Coherence, Fluency, Completeness, Equivalence, Groundedness; agent: IntentResolution, TaskAdherence, ToolCallAccuracy | per-call judge tokens | real `IChatClient` + `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1` | **ON** (stubbed until judge wired) |
   | NLP (zero-config sanity) | BLEU, GLEU, F1, Words | free | reference responses in golden.json | ON |
   | Safety | `ContentHarmEvaluator` (Hate+SelfHarm+Violence+Sexual single-shot), ProtectedMaterial, IndirectAttack, CodeVulnerability, UngroundedAttributes, GroundednessPro | Foundry evaluation service charges | Azure AI Foundry endpoint + `EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY=1` | **OFF** — prompt the user: "Wire safety evaluators too? # setup-maf-evals

Scaffold an `<App>.Evals.Tests` MSTest project that measures latency,
token usage, cost, quality, and safety on every change to a .NET
agentic app — and produces the proper Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation
HTML report by default.

## When to Use

- The user asks to "set up evals", "add an evaluation harness", "wire
  up MEAI evaluation", or "measure my agent's quality".
- The user wants to **validate quality** after a model change ("does
  swapping gpt-4o → gpt-4o-mini regress responses?") and needs a
  reproducible baseline.
- The user wants to **compare** model assignments side-by-side
  ("compare gpt-4o vs gpt-4o-mini across my agents").
- The user wants to **add safety evaluators** (Hate/Violence/SelfHarm/
  Sexual via Azure AI Foundry) to an existing agent.
- The user wants a recurring eval run wired into CI (the optional
  GitHub Actions workflow).

## When Not to Use

- The user wants a **one-shot audit** of existing code without scaffolding
  a new test project — use `scan-agentic-app-perf` instead.
- The user wants **always-on perf guard-rails** in the project's
  agent-instructions file — use `configure-agentic-perf-rules`.
- The project is not a .NET agentic app, or the user is not using
  `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` / `Microsoft.Agents.AI`.
- The user explicitly does not want an MSTest dependency and is not
  willing to use the opt-in `--shape console` runner.

## Supported topologies

The skill targets any .NET project using Microsoft Agent Framework
(`Microsoft.Agents.AI`), regardless of how it's hosted:

- **Aspire AppHost** (`*.AppHost.csproj` orchestrating agent services) — the
  most common shape; the generated `AgentChatClientFactory` mirrors the
  AppHost's connection-string-driven `IChatClient` registration.
- **Plain console / worker service** — `Microsoft.Agents.AI` registered
  directly against an OpenAI or Foundry client without an Aspire AppHost.
  The factory mirrors the app's direct registration (e.g. `AddOpenAIClient`
  or `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient` at the host level).
- **ASP.NET Core minimal API** — agents registered via the same DI patterns.

`IChatClient` detection (see `references/ichatclient-detection.md`) works
the same way across all topologies; only the AppHost-vs-Program.cs search
locations differ.

## Workflow

### 1. Discover the target app

Detect:

- Solution file (`*.sln` / `*.slnx`)
- AppHost project name (`*.AppHost.csproj`)
- Agent service projects
- Existing test / eval projects (avoid clobbering)
- **`IChatClient` registration** (scan AppHost + agent projects for
  `AddChatClient` / `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient` / `AddOllamaChatClient`
  / `AddOpenAIChatClient` and any explicit `services.AddSingleton<IChatClient>` or
  Foundry deployment alias references). See `references/ichatclient-detection.md`.

If no agentic app is detected, abort. If a `*.Evals.Tests` project already
exists, switch to update mode (see step 1a).

### 1a. Update mode (when `*.Evals.Tests` project already exists)

File classes:

| Class            | Files                                                                  | Behavior on update         |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| **infra**        | `*.Evals.Tests.csproj`, `dotnet-tools.json`, `Reporting/*`, `Wire/*`, test class skeletons | merge package refs; create file if missing; do **not** overwrite |
| **user data**    | `Quality/rubric.md`, `Quality/golden.json`, `Compare/matrix.json`, `Telemetry/inputs.json`, `Telemetry/prices.json`, `quality.thresholds.json`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml` | never overwrite; create if missing |
| **generated**    | `.copilot/perf-reports/evals/`                                         | regenerate freely          |

If an existing infra file differs from the current template, surface
the diff in the chat output but do not overwrite. Recommend the user
review and merge manually.

`golden.json` has a `schema_version` field. If the detected version is
older than the current template, offer to migrate (additive only —
preserves existing rows, adds the new fields as nullable).

### 2. Confirm scope with the user

Present the detection summary, then confirm:

1. **Project shape** (default: MSTest). Alternative: console runner
   (legacy v1 shape) — only emit if user explicitly asks for it.
2. **Evaluator categories to enable.** Defaults shown; user can override.

   | Category | Evaluators | Cost | Needs | Default |
   |------|-----------|------|-------|---------|
   | **Quality** *(headline)* | Relevance, Coherence, Fluency, Completeness, Equivalence, Groundedness; agent: IntentResolution, TaskAdherence, ToolCallAccuracy | per-call judge tokens | real `IChatClient` + `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1` | **ON** (stubbed until judge wired) |
   | NLP (zero-config sanity) | BLEU, GLEU, F1, Words | free | reference responses in golden.json | ON |
   | Safety | `ContentHarmEvaluator` (Hate+SelfHarm+Violence+Sexual single-shot), ProtectedMaterial, IndirectAttack, CodeVulnerability, UngroundedAttributes, GroundednessPro | Foundry evaluation service charges | Azure AI Foundry endpoint + `EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY=1` | **OFF** — prompt the user: "Wire safety evaluators too? (y/N)" |

   Frame Quality as the headline evaluation; NLP is the zero-config
   first-run experience that emits a real `report.html` before any
   creds exist; Safety is the opt-in for production-bound apps.

3. **IChatClient detection result.** Show what was detected (e.g., "Found
   `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient` in `AppHost.cs:41` with deployment alias `chat`").
   Ask the user to confirm or override. If detection failed, generate a
   stub factory the user will fill in.
4. **Run modes to scaffold.** Telemetry (default ON) and Quality (default
   ON). **Compare mode is opt-in** — prompt the user: "Wire compare
   mode for side-by-side matrix.json runs? (y/N)". Compare adds the
   largest scaffold (extra runner + matrix.json + delta-table generator)
   and is the least commonly used surface.
5. **Optional add-ons:** Aspire dashboard panel, GitHub Actions workflow.

### 3. Scaffold the project

See `references/project-template.md` for the file tree, csproj, and
`GlobalUsings.cs` template. The project is **MSTest** by default
(`<App>.Evals.Tests`); a console-runner shape is available behind an
explicit `--shape console` flag.

Always emit: `Reporting/{ReportingConfig.cs, Tier.cs, AievalReport.cs,
WordCountEvaluator.cs, MetricsGlossary.cs}`, `Wire/{AgentChatClientFactory.cs,
StubChatClient.cs}`, `Quality/{QualityTests.cs, rubric.md, golden.json}`,
`Telemetry/{TelemetryTests.cs, inputs.json, prices.json}`,
`quality.thresholds.json`, `GlobalUsings.cs`, `dotnet-tools.json`.
Emit `Compare/{CompareTests.cs, matrix.json}` only if the user opted into
compare mode (step 2 #4). Emit `Safety/SafetyTests.cs` and
`.github/workflows/evals.yml` only if the user opted in (steps 7 and 9).

After writing files:

```pwsh
dotnet sln <SolutionFile> add <App>.Evals.Tests/<App>.Evals.Tests.csproj
dotnet tool restore                  # installs aieval
# .gitignore additions
echo ".copilot/perf-reports/evals/`n<App>.Evals.Tests/_store/" >> .gitignore
```

### 4. Wire telemetry mode

See `references/telemetry-capture.md`. Default ON. Captures latency,
input/output tokens, and price-table-driven cost via a delegating
`IChatClient`. Writes `telemetry.{md,json,junit.xml}` next to
`report.html`. **Not** the MEAI HTML report — that's quality mode's job.

### 5. Wire quality mode

See `references/quality-modes.md`. Default ON. The **only** runner that
produces `report.html`. Uses `DiskBasedReportingConfiguration` +
`ScenarioRun.EvaluateAsync` + `[AssemblyCleanup]` invokes
`dotnet tool run aieval report`. Stub tier registers the 4 NLP
evaluators; judge tier (`EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1`) adds the LLM-as-judge
evaluators from `references/evaluators-catalog.md`.

### 6. Wire compare mode (opt-in)

See `references/compare-mode.md`. **Default OFF.** Only scaffold when
the user opted in at step 2 (#4). When enabled, reads `matrix.json`;
each entry runs through the **same** `ReportingConfiguration` with a
distinct `executionName`, so `aieval report` aggregates the comparison
columns into a single HTML view. Also writes a `compare.md` delta
table.

### 7. Wire safety mode (opt-in)

See `references/safety-mode.md`. **Default OFF.** When enabled, adds
`Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.Safety` and emits `SafetyTests.cs`
with `ContentHarmEvaluator` (single-shot 4-metric bundle), plus
ProtectedMaterial / IndirectAttack / CodeVulnerability /
UngroundedAttributes. Skipped at runtime via `Assert.Inconclusive`
when `EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY` is unset — never fails the build for
missing creds.

### 8. Optional Aspire panel (apply mode)

See `references/aspire-dashboard-panel.md`. Default OFF; modifies
the AppHost project. To enable, user must say "wire the panel" /
equivalent. Always show a unified diff + ask for confirmation before
writing AppHost edits.

### 9. Optional CI workflow (opt-in)

See `references/ci-workflow.md`. Default OFF. Emits
`.github/workflows/evals.yml` that runs `dotnet test` on every PR,
auto-detects tier from repo secrets (`AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` →
judge; `AZURE_AI_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT` → safety), and uploads
`report.html` as a workflow artifact.

### 10. Validation

- `dotnet build <App>.Evals.Tests.csproj` exits 0.
- `dotnet test <App>.Evals.Tests.csproj` exits 0 in stub tier (no creds needed).
  - Stub tier must emit a `report.html` with **≥ 4 distinct metric columns**
    (Words, BLEU, GLEU, F1) across all scenarios in golden.json.
  - All scenarios must produce non-null metric values (no "—" placeholders).
- If `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1` and an `IChatClient` is wired,
  `dotnet test` must additionally produce ≥ 3 Quality metrics (Relevance,
  Coherence, Fluency).

### 11. Surface in chat

Lead with **Quality** as the headline evaluation; frame NLP as the
zero-config sanity check and Safety/Compare as additions.

1. **Quality (headline).** State whether the judge is wired:
   - *Stubbed* — "Quality scaffolded; judge will run once you wire
     `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1` + a chat endpoint. The next block tells
     you how."
   - *Live* — "Quality judge active against `<deployment>`; report
     shows Relevance / Coherence / Fluency / Completeness / Equivalence."
   - Caveat the user **must** know up-front: *"The built-in Quality
     rubrics are generic. Agents with deliberate stylistic constraints
     (brevity, persona, format adherence) will score low on
     Completeness / Equivalence even when working as designed. See
     `references/common-pitfalls.md#tuning-quality-for-stylistic-agents`
     for the per-app override pattern."*
2. **Promoting Quality to the judge tier.** If the app's `IChatClient`
   reads from a connection string (Aspire pattern), include the exact
   two commands:

   ```pwsh
   dotnet user-secrets init --project <App>.Evals.Tests
   dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:<alias>" `
     "Endpoint=https://<host>.services.ai.azure.com/models;DeploymentId=<alias>" `
     --project <App>.Evals.Tests
   # then: $env:EVAL_USE_REAL_AGENT="1"; $env:EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE="1"; dotnet test
   ```

   Note the **three** endpoint gotchas: (a) hostname strips dashes on
   some resources, (b) key auth is often disabled → drop the `Key=`
   segment and rely on `DefaultAzureCredential`, (c) **the judge
   deployment must be a non-reasoning model** (gpt-4o / gpt-4o-mini /
   gpt-4-turbo). Reasoning models (gpt-5*, o-series) reject `max_tokens`
   with HTTP 400 and MEAI silently records that as a per-metric error
   row. If the production model is a reasoning one, set
   `EVAL_JUDGE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME=<non-reasoning-alias>` so the judge
   points at a different deployment than the agent. Full details in
   `references/ichatclient-detection.md`.
3. **NLP (zero-config sanity).** "`report.html` already populates with
   Words / BLEU / GLEU / F1 from `golden.json` without any creds — run
   `dotnet test` now to see it."
4. **Additional categories you can wire.** List Safety
   (`EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY=1`, opt-in scaffold) and Compare (re-run
   the skill with `compare: true` if it wasn't opted in originally)
   as one-line bullets — not in the main flow.
5. **Paths.** Project path, `report.html` path, **glossary path**
   (`metrics-glossary.md` co-located with `report.html`), persistent
   `_store/` path.
6. **CLI invocations.** `dotnet test`, `dotnet tool run aieval report`,
   and the IChatClient detection result so the user knows what was
   auto-wired.
7. **Follow-up recommendation.** "Re-run after swapping a model per
   rule #3 of `configure-agentic-perf-rules` to confirm no quality
   regression."
8. **Cache payoff.** "First `dotnet test` populates `_store/cache/` and
   takes the full ~60s. Every subsequent run against unchanged inputs
   reuses cached agent + judge responses — typically ~5s with zero LLM
   cost. The Diagnostic Data section of `report.html` shows per-call
   Hit/Miss. To force a fresh run, delete `_store/cache/` or change the
   rubric / golden inputs."

Also link `references/evaluators-catalog.md` and
`references/metrics-glossary.md` so the user can see what each metric
means.

## Common pitfalls

See `references/common-pitfalls.md`.

# setup-maf-evals

- The user wants to **validate quality** after a model change ("does

  reproducible baseline.
- The user wants to **compare** model assignments side-by-side
  ("compare gpt-4o vs gpt-4o-mini across my agents").
- The user wants to **add safety evaluators** (Hate/Violence/SelfHarm/

- The user wants a recurring eval run wired into CI (the optional
  GitHub Actions workflow).

## When Not to Use

- The user wants a **one-shot audit** of existing code without scaffolding
  a new test project — use `scan-agentic-app-perf` instead.
- The user wants **always-on perf guard-rails** in the project's
  agent-instructions file — use `configure-agentic-perf-rules`.
- The project is not a .NET agentic app, or the user is not using
  `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` / `Microsoft.Agents.AI`.
- The user explicitly does not want an MSTest dependency and is not
  willing to use the opt-in `--shape console` runner.

(`Microsoft.Agents.AI`), regardless of how it's hosted:

  most common shape; the generated `AgentChatClientFactory` mirrors the

  or `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient` at the host level).

locations differ.

# setup-maf-evals

Scaffold an `<App>.Evals.Tests` MSTest project that measures latency,
token usage, cost, quality, and safety on every change to a .NET
agentic app — and produces the proper Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation
HTML report by default.

## When to Use

- The user asks to "set up evals", "add an evaluation harness", "wire
  up MEAI evaluation", or "measure my agent's quality".
- The user wants to **validate quality** after a model change ("does
  swapping gpt-4o → gpt-4o-mini regress responses?") and needs a
  reproducible baseline.
- The user wants to **compare** model assignments side-by-side
  ("compare gpt-4o vs gpt-4o-mini across my agents").
- The user wants to **add safety evaluators** (Hate/Violence/SelfHarm/
  Sexual via Azure AI Foundry) to an existing agent.
- The user wants a recurring eval run wired into CI (the optional
  GitHub Actions workflow).

## When Not to Use

- The user wants a **one-shot audit** of existing code without scaffolding
  a new test project — use `scan-agentic-app-perf` instead.
- The user wants **always-on perf guard-rails** in the project's
  agent-instructions file — use `configure-agentic-perf-rules`.
- The project is not a .NET agentic app, or the user is not using
  `Microsoft.Extensions.AI` / `Microsoft.Agents.AI`.
- The user explicitly does not want an MSTest dependency and is not
  willing to use the opt-in `--shape console` runner.

## Supported topologies

The skill targets any .NET project using Microsoft Agent Framework
(`Microsoft.Agents.AI`), regardless of how it's hosted:

- **Aspire AppHost** (`*.AppHost.csproj` orchestrating agent services) — the
  most common shape; the generated `AgentChatClientFactory` mirrors the
  AppHost's connection-string-driven `IChatClient` registration.
- **Plain console / worker service** — `Microsoft.Agents.AI` registered
  directly against an OpenAI or Foundry client without an Aspire AppHost.
  The factory mirrors the app's direct registration (e.g. `AddOpenAIClient`
  or `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient` at the host level).
- **ASP.NET Core minimal API** — agents registered via the same DI patterns.

`IChatClient` detection (see `references/ichatclient-detection.md`) works
the same way across all topologies; only the AppHost-vs-Program.cs search
locations differ.

## Workflow

### 1. Discover the target app

Detect:

- Solution file (`*.sln` / `*.slnx`)
- AppHost project name (`*.AppHost.csproj`)
- Agent service projects
- Existing test / eval projects (avoid clobbering)
- **`IChatClient` registration** (scan AppHost + agent projects for
  `AddChatClient` / `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient` / `AddOllamaChatClient`
  / `AddOpenAIChatClient` and any explicit `services.AddSingleton<IChatClient>` or
  Foundry deployment alias references). See `references/ichatclient-detection.md`.

If no agentic app is detected, abort. If a `*.Evals.Tests` project already
exists, switch to update mode (see step 1a).

### 1a. Update mode (when `*.Evals.Tests` project already exists)

File classes:

| Class            | Files                                                                  | Behavior on update         |
|------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------|
| **infra**        | `*.Evals.Tests.csproj`, `dotnet-tools.json`, `Reporting/*`, `Wire/*`, test class skeletons | merge package refs; create file if missing; do **not** overwrite |
| **user data**    | `Quality/rubric.md`, `Quality/golden.json`, `Compare/matrix.json`, `Telemetry/inputs.json`, `Telemetry/prices.json`, `quality.thresholds.json`, `.github/workflows/evals.yml` | never overwrite; create if missing |
| **generated**    | `.copilot/perf-reports/evals/`                                         | regenerate freely          |

If an existing infra file differs from the current template, surface
the diff in the chat output but do not overwrite. Recommend the user
review and merge manually.

`golden.json` has a `schema_version` field. If the detected version is
older than the current template, offer to migrate (additive only —
preserves existing rows, adds the new fields as nullable).

### 2. Confirm scope with the user

Present the detection summary, then confirm:

1. **Project shape** (default: MSTest). Alternative: console runner
   (legacy v1 shape) — only emit if user explicitly asks for it.
2. **Evaluator categories to enable.** Defaults shown; user can override.

   | Category | Evaluators | Cost | Needs | Default |
   |------|-----------|------|-------|---------|
   | **Quality** *(headline)* | Relevance, Coherence, Fluency, Completeness, Equivalence, Groundedness; agent: IntentResolution, TaskAdherence, ToolCallAccuracy | per-call judge tokens | real `IChatClient` + `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1` | **ON** (stubbed until judge wired) |
   | NLP (zero-config sanity) | BLEU, GLEU, F1, Words | free | reference responses in golden.json | ON |
   | Safety | `ContentHarmEvaluator` (Hate+SelfHarm+Violence+Sexual single-shot), ProtectedMaterial, IndirectAttack, CodeVulnerability, UngroundedAttributes, GroundednessPro | Foundry evaluation service charges | Azure AI Foundry endpoint + `EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY=1` | **OFF** — prompt the user: "Wire safety evaluators too? (y/N)" |

   Frame Quality as the headline evaluation; NLP is the zero-config
   first-run experience that emits a real `report.html` before any
   creds exist; Safety is the opt-in for production-bound apps.

3. **IChatClient detection result.** Show what was detected (e.g., "Found
   `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient` in `AppHost.cs:41` with deployment alias `chat`").
   Ask the user to confirm or override. If detection failed, generate a
   stub factory the user will fill in.
4. **Run modes to scaffold.** Telemetry (default ON) and Quality (default
   ON). **Compare mode is opt-in** — prompt the user: "Wire compare
   mode for side-by-side matrix.json runs? (y/N)". Compare adds the
   largest scaffold (extra runner + matrix.json + delta-table generator)
   and is the least commonly used surface.
5. **Optional add-ons:** Aspire dashboard panel, GitHub Actions workflow.

### 3. Scaffold the project

See `references/project-template.md` for the file tree, csproj, and
`GlobalUsings.cs` template. The project is **MSTest** by default
(`<App>.Evals.Tests`); a console-runner shape is available behind an
explicit `--shape console` flag.

Always emit: `Reporting/{ReportingConfig.cs, Tier.cs, AievalReport.cs,
WordCountEvaluator.cs, MetricsGlossary.cs}`, `Wire/{AgentChatClientFactory.cs,
StubChatClient.cs}`, `Quality/{QualityTests.cs, rubric.md, golden.json}`,
`Telemetry/{TelemetryTests.cs, inputs.json, prices.json}`,
`quality.thresholds.json`, `GlobalUsings.cs`, `dotnet-tools.json`.
Emit `Compare/{CompareTests.cs, matrix.json}` only if the user opted into
compare mode (step 2 #4). Emit `Safety/SafetyTests.cs` and
`.github/workflows/evals.yml` only if the user opted in (steps 7 and 9).

After writing files:

```pwsh
dotnet sln <SolutionFile> add <App>.Evals.Tests/<App>.Evals.Tests.csproj
dotnet tool restore                  # installs aieval
# .gitignore additions
echo ".copilot/perf-reports/evals/`n<App>.Evals.Tests/_store/" >> .gitignore
```

### 4. Wire telemetry mode

See `references/telemetry-capture.md`. Default ON. Captures latency,
input/output tokens, and price-table-driven cost via a delegating
`IChatClient`. Writes `telemetry.{md,json,junit.xml}` next to
`report.html`. **Not** the MEAI HTML report — that's quality mode's job.

### 5. Wire quality mode

See `references/quality-modes.md`. Default ON. The **only** runner that
produces `report.html`. Uses `DiskBasedReportingConfiguration` +
`ScenarioRun.EvaluateAsync` + `[AssemblyCleanup]` invokes
`dotnet tool run aieval report`. Stub tier registers the 4 NLP
evaluators; judge tier (`EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1`) adds the LLM-as-judge
evaluators from `references/evaluators-catalog.md`.

### 6. Wire compare mode (opt-in)

See `references/compare-mode.md`. **Default OFF.** Only scaffold when
the user opted in at step 2 (#4). When enabled, reads `matrix.json`;
each entry runs through the **same** `ReportingConfiguration` with a
distinct `executionName`, so `aieval report` aggregates the comparison
columns into a single HTML view. Also writes a `compare.md` delta
table.

### 7. Wire safety mode (opt-in)

See `references/safety-mode.md`. **Default OFF.** When enabled, adds
`Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.Safety` and emits `SafetyTests.cs`
with `ContentHarmEvaluator` (single-shot 4-metric bundle), plus
ProtectedMaterial / IndirectAttack / CodeVulnerability /
UngroundedAttributes. Skipped at runtime via `Assert.Inconclusive`
when `EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY` is unset — never fails the build for
missing creds.

### 8. Optional Aspire panel (apply mode)

See `references/aspire-dashboard-panel.md`. Default OFF; modifies
the AppHost project. To enable, user must say "wire the panel" /
equivalent. Always show a unified diff + ask for confirmation before
writing AppHost edits.

### 9. Optional CI workflow (opt-in)

See `references/ci-workflow.md`. Default OFF. Emits
`.github/workflows/evals.yml` that runs `dotnet test` on every PR,
auto-detects tier from repo secrets (`AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT` →
judge; `AZURE_AI_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT` → safety), and uploads
`report.html` as a workflow artifact.

### 10. Validation

- `dotnet build <App>.Evals.Tests.csproj` exits 0.
- `dotnet test <App>.Evals.Tests.csproj` exits 0 in stub tier (no creds needed).
  - Stub tier must emit a `report.html` with **≥ 4 distinct metric columns**
    (Words, BLEU, GLEU, F1) across all scenarios in golden.json.
  - All scenarios must produce non-null metric values (no "—" placeholders).
- If `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1` and an `IChatClient` is wired,
  `dotnet test` must additionally produce ≥ 3 Quality metrics (Relevance,
  Coherence, Fluency).

### 11. Surface in chat

Lead with **Quality** as the headline evaluation; frame NLP as the
zero-config sanity check and Safety/Compare as additions.

1. **Quality (headline).** State whether the judge is wired:
   - *Stubbed* — "Quality scaffolded; judge will run once you wire
     `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1` + a chat endpoint. The next block tells
     you how."
   - *Live* — "Quality judge active against `<deployment>`; report
     shows Relevance / Coherence / Fluency / Completeness / Equivalence."
   - Caveat the user **must** know up-front: *"The built-in Quality
     rubrics are generic. Agents with deliberate stylistic constraints
     (brevity, persona, format adherence) will score low on
     Completeness / Equivalence even when working as designed. See
     `references/common-pitfalls.md#tuning-quality-for-stylistic-agents`
     for the per-app override pattern."*
2. **Promoting Quality to the judge tier.** If the app's `IChatClient`
   reads from a connection string (Aspire pattern), include the exact
   two commands:

   ```pwsh
   dotnet user-secrets init --project <App>.Evals.Tests
   dotnet user-secrets set "ConnectionStrings:<alias>" `
     "Endpoint=https://<host>.services.ai.azure.com/models;DeploymentId=<alias>" `
     --project <App>.Evals.Tests
   # then: $env:EVAL_USE_REAL_AGENT="1"; $env:EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE="1"; dotnet test
   ```

   Note the **three** endpoint gotchas: (a) hostname strips dashes on
   some resources, (b) key auth is often disabled → drop the `Key=`
   segment and rely on `DefaultAzureCredential`, (c) **the judge
   deployment must be a non-reasoning model** (gpt-4o / gpt-4o-mini /
   gpt-4-turbo). Reasoning models (gpt-5*, o-series) reject `max_tokens`
   with HTTP 400 and MEAI silently records that as a per-metric error
   row. If the production model is a reasoning one, set
   `EVAL_JUDGE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME=<non-reasoning-alias>` so the judge
   points at a different deployment than the agent. Full details in
   `references/ichatclient-detection.md`.
3. **NLP (zero-config sanity).** "`report.html` already populates with
   Words / BLEU / GLEU / F1 from `golden.json` without any creds — run
   `dotnet test` now to see it."
4. **Additional categories you can wire.** List Safety
   (`EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY=1`, opt-in scaffold) and Compare (re-run
   the skill with `compare: true` if it wasn't opted in originally)
   as one-line bullets — not in the main flow.
5. **Paths.** Project path, `report.html` path, **glossary path**
   (`metrics-glossary.md` co-located with `report.html`), persistent
   `_store/` path.
6. **CLI invocations.** `dotnet test`, `dotnet tool run aieval report`,
   and the IChatClient detection result so the user knows what was
   auto-wired.
7. **Follow-up recommendation.** "Re-run after swapping a model per
   rule #3 of `configure-agentic-perf-rules` to confirm no quality
   regression."
8. **Cache payoff.** "First `dotnet test` populates `_store/cache/` and
   takes the full ~60s. Every subsequent run against unchanged inputs
   reuses cached agent + judge responses — typically ~5s with zero LLM
   cost. The Diagnostic Data section of `report.html` shows per-call
   Hit/Miss. To force a fresh run, delete `_store/cache/` or change the
   rubric / golden inputs."

Also link `references/evaluators-catalog.md` and
`references/metrics-glossary.md` so the user can see what each metric
means.

## Common pitfalls

See `references/common-pitfalls.md`.

## References

- `references/project-template.md` — file tree + `.csproj` layout.
- `references/ichatclient-detection.md` — registration scan + factory emission.
- `references/evaluators-catalog.md` — NLP + Quality + Safety catalog with required `EvaluationContext` types.
- `references/metrics-glossary.md` — per-run glossary content + `MetricsGlossary.cs` template.
- `references/telemetry-capture.md` — per-call hook + cost report format.

- `references/compare-mode.md` — `matrix.json` + per-entry `executionName`.
- `references/safety-mode.md` — opt-in safety scaffold + `ContentHarmEvaluator` default.
- `references/ci-workflow.md` — `.github/workflows/evals.yml` template.
- `references/aspire-dashboard-panel.md` — optional static-file panel.
- `references/common-pitfalls.md` — known footguns to avoid when scaffolding.

11. directories**. Match (case-insensitive, multi-line):
12. 
13. | Pattern (regex-ish) | Inferred client | Example file:line |
14. |---------------------|-----------------|--------------------|
15. | `AddAzureOpenAIChatClient\s*\(` or `AddAzureOpenAIClient\s*\(` | Azure OpenAI | `AppHost.cs`, `Program.cs` |
16. | `AddOpenAIChatClient\s*\(` | OpenAI direct | `Program.cs` |
17. | `AddOllamaChatClient\s*\(` | Ollama | `Program.cs` |

20. | `AddOpenAIClient\s*\([^)]*\)\s*\.AddChatClient\s*\(` | Aspire OpenAI/v1 (Foundry-routed via the OpenAI SDK) | `Program.cs` |
21. | `services\.AddSingleton<IChatClient>` (any explicit registration) | custom | varies |
22. | `\.AsIChatClient\(\)` (after an SDK client) | manual wrap | varies |

25. > Aspire 13.2 way of wiring an `IChatClient` against a Foundry chat
26. > deployment via the `Azure.AI.Inference` beta SDK. The argument is the
27. > **connection-string name**, which Aspire's AppHost populates
28. > automatically (`AddDeployment("chat", ...)` -> connection string `chat`).
29. > The factory mirrors both calls verbatim.

31. > ⚠️ **Deprecation note (as of 2026):** the `Azure.AI.Inference` beta SDK
32. > is being retired on **August 26, 2026** in favor of the GA OpenAI/v1
33. > API + stable OpenAI SDK. New apps should prefer the
34. > `AddOpenAIClient(...).AddChatClient(...)` pattern against an OpenAI/v1
35. > endpoint, which avoids several quirks (notably the reasoning-model
36. > `max_tokens` rejection documented in
37. > `references/common-pitfalls.md`). The skill still detects and supports

 | `AddOpenAIChatClient\s*\(` | OpenAI direct | `Program.cs` |
 | `AddOllamaChatClient\s*\(` | Ollama | `Program.cs` |
 | `AddAIInference\s*\(` (Foundry deployment alias) | Azure AI Foundry | `AppHost.cs` |

 | `services\.AddSingleton<IChatClient>` (any explicit registration) | custom | varies |

 > Aspire 13.2 way of wiring an `IChatClient` against a Foundry chat

1. # Telemetry mode
2. 
3. Telemetry mode captures **latency, input tokens, output tokens, and
4. cost** per agent call across a fixed input set. It is **not** the same
5. as the MEAI eval report — it produces a separate cost/latency capture.
6. 
7. ## Why separate from quality
8. 
9. Quality mode answers "is the response any good?" via
10. `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.Reporting` and produces
11. `report.html`.
12. 
13. Telemetry mode answers "how much does it cost and how slow is it?"
14. via a delegating `IChatClient` wrapper. Different question, different
15. artifact. Conflating them is the #1 most common scaffolding mistake.
16. 
17. ## Artifacts (each in `.copilot/perf-reports/evals/<timestamp>/`)
18. 
19. - `telemetry.md` — human-readable per-input table.
20. - `telemetry.json` — machine-readable for CI scraping.
21. - `telemetry.junit.xml` — for test-result dashboards.
22. 
23. These are **distinct** from `report.html` (which only quality mode
24. writes). The skill output should never refer to `telemetry.md` as
25. "the eval report."
26. 
27. ## Test shape
28. 
29. ```csharp
30. [TestClass]
31. public sealed class TelemetryTests
32. {
33.     public static IEnumerable<object[]> Inputs() =>
34.         InputsLoader.Load().Select(i => new object[] { i });
35. 
36.     [TestMethod, DynamicData(nameof(Inputs), DynamicDataSourceType.Method)]
37.     public async Task Capture(TelemetryInput input)
38.     {
39.         var inner = Wire.ResolveAgentClient();
40.         var wrapped = new TelemetryCapturingChatClient(inner, PriceTable.Load());
41. 
42.         var messages = new List<ChatMessage> { new(ChatRole.User, input.Text) };
43.         var sw = Stopwatch.StartNew();
44.         var response = await wrapped.GetResponseAsync(messages);
45.         sw.Stop();
46. 
47.         TelemetryStore.Record(new TelemetryRecord(
48.             AgentName: input.Agent,
49.             Model: response.ModelId ?? "unknown",
50.             InputTokens:  response.Usage?.InputTokenCount  ?? 0,
51.             OutputTokens: response.Usage?.OutputTokenCount ?? 0,
52.             LatencyMs: sw.ElapsedMilliseconds,
53.             CostUsd: wrapped.LastCostUsd));
54.     }
55. 
56.     [ClassCleanup]
57.     public static void WriteReports() => TelemetryStore.FlushTo(
58.         Path.Combine(RepoRoot.Find(), ".copilot", "perf-reports", "evals",
59.                      ReportingConfig.ExecutionName));
60. }
61. ```
62. 
63. ## Delegating client (sketch)
64. 
65. ```csharp
66. internal sealed class TelemetryCapturingChatClient(IChatClient inner, PriceTable prices) : IChatClient
67. {
68.     public decimal LastCostUsd { get; private set; }
69. 
70.     public async Task<ChatResponse> GetResponseAsync(
71.         IEnumerable<ChatMessage> messages, ChatOptions? options = null,
72.         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
73.     {
74.         var resp = await inner.GetResponseAsync(messages, options, cancellationToken);
75.         var usage = resp.Usage;
76.         LastCostUsd = prices.Cost(resp.ModelId,
77.             usage?.InputTokenCount ?? 0, usage?.OutputTokenCount ?? 0);
78.         return resp;
79.     }
80. 
81.     // GetStreamingResponseAsync delegates similarly; usage parsed off the last update.
82. 
83.     public object? GetService(Type serviceType, object? serviceKey = null) =>
84.         inner.GetService(serviceType, serviceKey);
85. 
86.     public void Dispose() => inner.Dispose();
87. }
88. ```
89. 
90. ## `inputs.json`
91. 
92. ```json
93. [
94.   { "agent": "receptionist", "text": "Hi" },
95.   { "agent": "behavioural",  "text": "Tell me about a tough project" },
96.   { "agent": "technical",    "text": "How would you throttle requests?" },
97.   { "agent": "summariser",   "text": "Wrap up the interview" }
98. ]
99. ```
100. 
101. ## `prices.json`
102. 
103. ```json
104. {
105.   "gpt-4o-mini": { "input_per_1k": 0.00015, "output_per_1k": 0.0006 },
106.   "gpt-4o":      { "input_per_1k": 0.0025,  "output_per_1k": 0.01   },
107.   "o4-mini":     { "input_per_1k": 0.003,   "output_per_1k": 0.012  }
108. }
109. ```
110. 
111. Edit freely — costs change. The price table is **never** baked into source.
112. 
113. ## `InputsLoader` (the deserializer the test uses)
114. 
115. `inputs.json` is snake_case; the C# records (`TelemetryInput`, etc.) are
116. PascalCase. The loader **must** specify a `JsonSerializerOptions` with
117. `PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower` and
118. `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true`, or properties deserialize to
119. `null` and tests fail (or, worse, silently produce zeroed records when
120. the property is never read — telemetry mode is especially prone to
121. this because it never accesses some fields).
122. 
123. ```csharp
124. internal static class InputsLoader
125. {
126.     private static readonly JsonSerializerOptions s_options = new()
127.     {
128.         PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower,
129.         PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true,
130.     };
131. 
132.     public static List<TelemetryInput> Load()
133.     {
134.         var path = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Telemetry", "inputs.json");
135.         return JsonSerializer.Deserialize<List<TelemetryInput>>(
136.             File.ReadAllText(path), s_options) ?? new();
137.     }
138. }
139. ```
140. 
141. Same applies to `PriceTable.Load()` (`prices.json`), `MatrixLoader.Load()`
142. (`matrix.json`), and `GoldenLoader.Load()` (`golden.json`). Use a shared
143. options instance — do NOT rely on STJ defaults.
144.

113. ## `InputsLoader` (the deserializer the test uses)
114. 
115. `inputs.json` is snake_case; the C# records (`TelemetryInput`, etc.) are
116. PascalCase. The loader **must** specify a `JsonSerializerOptions` with
117. `PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower` and
118. `PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true`, or properties deserialize to
119. `null` and tests fail (or, worse, silently produce zeroed records when
120. the property is never read — telemetry mode is especially prone to
121. this because it never accesses some fields).
122. 
123. ```csharp
124. internal static class InputsLoader
125. {
126.     private static readonly JsonSerializerOptions s_options = new()
127.     {
128.         PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.SnakeCaseLower,
129.         PropertyNameCaseInsensitive = true,
130.     };
131. 
132.     public static List<TelemetryInput> Load()
133.     {
134.         var path = Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Telemetry", "inputs.json");
135.         return JsonSerializer.Deserialize<List<TelemetryInput>>(
136.             File.ReadAllText(path), s_options) ?? new();
137.     }

140. 
141. Same applies to `PriceTable.Load()` (`prices.json`), `MatrixLoader.Load()`
142. (`matrix.json`), and `GoldenLoader.Load()` (`golden.json`). Use a shared
143. options instance — do NOT rely on STJ defaults.

1. # Quality mode
2. 
3. `Quality/QualityTests.cs` is the MSTest class that actually drives
4. `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.Reporting`. It's the **only**
5. runner that produces `report.html`.
6. 
7. ## Response cache (read first)
8. 
9. `DiskBasedReportingConfiguration.Create(..., enableResponseCaching: true)`
10. wraps the supplied `IChatClient` with a content-addressable cache stored
11. under `_store/cache/`. The first `dotnet test` run populates it; every
12. subsequent run against the same scenarios is **near-instant with zero
13. LLM cost** because both the agent call and the judge call are served
14. from disk.
15. 
16. Two rules MUST be followed to make the cache work:
17. 
18. 1. **The agent call must go through `run.ChatConfiguration!.ChatClient`**
19.    (NOT `Wire.ResolveAgentClient()` directly). The run-scoped client is
20.    the cached wrapper. Calling the factory directly bypasses the cache.
21. 2. **Do not pass a per-run `executionName`** to `Create(...)`. The
22.    `executionName` is part of the cache scope; a fresh timestamp per run
23.    guarantees misses. Use a separate `EvalEnv.ReportFolder` value for
24.    the report-output directory if you want per-run history.
25. 
26. If both rules are followed, the only legitimate reasons to see Miss in
27. the report's Diagnostic Data section are: (a) the cache directory was
28. deleted, (b) the rubric / golden / scenario input changed, (c) the
29. judge model or chat options changed, or (d) it's the first run.
30. 
31. ## Pipeline
32. 
33. ```
34. [ClassInitialize]  → build ReportingConfig (tier-aware evaluator list)
35. [TestMethod]       → one per golden.json entry
36.                      ├─ CreateScenarioRunAsync(scenarioName)
37.                      ├─ get cached IChatClient from run.ChatConfiguration
38.                      ├─ get agent response (cached)
39.                      ├─ build per-evaluator EvaluationContext (BLEU refs, F1 ground truth, ...)
40.                      └─ scenarioRun.EvaluateAsync(messages, response, contexts)  // judge calls cached
41. [AssemblyCleanup]  → dotnet tool run aieval report --path _store --output <ts>/report.html
42. ```
43. 
44. ## Reporting config (sketch)
45. 
46. ```csharp
47. // Reporting/ReportingConfig.cs
48. internal static class ReportingConfig
49. {
50.     public static readonly string StorageRoot =
51.         Path.Combine(RepoRoot.Find(), "_store");
52. 
53.     public static ReportingConfiguration ForQuality()
54.     {
55.         // ONE client serves both the agent call and the judge call. MEAI wraps
56.         // it with the response cache when handed to ChatConfiguration, so the
57.         // *agent* call gets cached too when QualityTests calls it through
58.         // `run.ChatConfiguration!.ChatClient` (see "Test class" below).
59.         // On re-runs against unchanged inputs, the entire run is a cache hit
60.         // and finishes in seconds with zero LLM cost. Override the judge with
61.         // a separate model via EVAL_JUDGE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME (advanced).
62.         var agent = Wire.ResolveAgentClient();
63.         var judge = Wire.ResolveJudgeClient(agent);
64. 
65.         var evaluators = new List<IEvaluator>
66.         {
67.             // Tier 1 — always on, deterministic
68.             new WordCountEvaluator(),
69.             new BLEUEvaluator(),
70.             new GLEUEvaluator(),
71.             new F1Evaluator(),
72.         };
73. 
74.         if (EvalEnv.UseRealJudge)
75.         {
76.             // Tier 2 — needs real judge
77.             evaluators.Add(new RelevanceEvaluator());
78.             evaluators.Add(new CoherenceEvaluator());
79.             evaluators.Add(new FluencyEvaluator());
80.             evaluators.Add(new CompletenessEvaluator());
81.             evaluators.Add(new EquivalenceEvaluator());
82.             evaluators.Add(new GroundednessEvaluator());
83. 
84.             if (AgenticAppDetected)
85.             {
86.                 evaluators.Add(new IntentResolutionEvaluator());
87.                 evaluators.Add(new TaskAdherenceEvaluator());
88.                 evaluators.Add(new ToolCallAccuracyEvaluator());
89.             }
90.         }
91. 
92.         // executionName: deliberately omitted. MEAI's default keeps the cache
93.         // scope stable across runs so re-runs hit. The report folder
94.         // timestamp lives separately in EvalEnv.ReportFolder.
95.         return DiskBasedReportingConfiguration.Create(
96.             storageRootPath: StorageRoot,
97.             evaluators: evaluators,
98.             chatConfiguration: new ChatConfiguration(judge),
99.             enableResponseCaching: true);
100.     }
101. }
102. ```
103. 
104. ## Test class (sketch)
105. 
106. ```csharp
107. [TestClass]
108. public sealed class QualityTests
109. {
110.     private static ReportingConfiguration s_reporting = null!;
111. 
112.     [ClassInitialize]
113.     public static void Init(TestContext _) =>
114.         s_reporting = ReportingConfig.ForQuality();
115. 
116.     public static IEnumerable<object[]> Golden() =>
117.         GoldenLoader.Load().Select(g => new object[] { g });
118. 
119.     [TestMethod, DynamicData(nameof(Golden), DynamicDataSourceType.Method)]
120.     public async Task Evaluate(GoldenItem g)
121.     {
122.         var scenarioName = $"{nameof(QualityTests)}.{g.Id}";
123.         await using var run = await s_reporting.CreateScenarioRunAsync(scenarioName);
124. 
125.         // IMPORTANT: use the run's ChatClient, NOT Wire.ResolveAgentClient(),
126.         // for the agent call. The run-scoped client is wrapped with MEAI's
127.         // response cache (set up by ReportingConfig.ForQuality), so identical
128.         // inputs across runs return cached responses instead of paying for
129.         // a fresh LLM call. Calling AgentChatClientFactory directly bypasses
130.         // the cache and guarantees a cache miss on every judge call too
131.         // (judge cache key includes the agent response, which then varies).
132.         //
133.         // EDGE CASE: when EVAL_JUDGE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME splits judge from agent,
134.         // run.ChatConfiguration.ChatClient IS the judge client — using it as
135.         // the agent would silently call the wrong model. Fall back to the
136.         // uncached agent factory in that case (judge calls still cache).
137.         var agent = string.IsNullOrEmpty(
138.             Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("EVAL_JUDGE_DEPLOYMENT_NAME"))
139.                 ? run.ChatConfiguration!.ChatClient
140.                 : Wire.ResolveAgentClient();
141.         var messages = new List<ChatMessage>
142.         {
143.             new(ChatRole.System, RubricLoader.SystemPrompt()),
144.             new(ChatRole.User, g.UserMessage),
145.         };
146.         var response = await agent.GetResponseAsync(messages);
147. 
148.         var contexts = new List<EvaluationContext>();
149.         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(g.ReferenceResponse))
150.         {
151.             contexts.Add(new BLEUEvaluatorContext(new[] { g.ReferenceResponse }));
152.             contexts.Add(new GLEUEvaluatorContext(new[] { g.ReferenceResponse }));
153.             contexts.Add(new F1EvaluatorContext(g.ReferenceResponse));
154.             contexts.Add(new EquivalenceEvaluatorContext(g.ReferenceResponse));
155.             contexts.Add(new CompletenessEvaluatorContext(g.ReferenceResponse));
156.         }
157.         if (!string.IsNullOrEmpty(g.Context))
158.             contexts.Add(new GroundednessEvaluatorContext(g.Context));
159. 
160.         var result = await run.EvaluateAsync(messages, response, contexts);
161.         Thresholds.ApplyOrLog(result, g.Id);  // hard_fail in JSON => Assert.Fail
162.     }
163. }
164. ```

169. // Reporting/AievalReport.cs
170. [TestClass]
171. public static class AievalReport
172. {
173.     [AssemblyCleanup]
174.     public static void GenerateReport()

177.             RepoRoot.Find(), ".copilot", "perf-reports", "evals",
178.             EvalEnv.ReportFolder);
179.         Directory.CreateDirectory(outDir);

181.

184.         {
185.             WorkingDirectory = RepoRoot.Find(),

187.             RedirectStandardError = true,
188.             UseShellExecute = false,
189.             CreateNoWindow = true,
190.         };
191.         using var p = Process.Start(psi)!;
192.         p.WaitForExit();
193.         Console.WriteLine($"Eval report: {html}");
194.     }
195. }
196. ```

198. ## EvalEnv (sketch, in `Reporting/Tier.cs`)
199. 
200. ```csharp
201. internal static class EvalEnv
202. {
203.     public static bool UseRealAgent =>
204.         Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("EVAL_USE_REAL_AGENT") == "1";
205. 
206.     public static bool UseRealJudge =>
207.         Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE") == "1";
208. 
209.     public static bool UseFoundrySafety =>
210.         Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY") == "1";
211. 
212.     public static string Tier =>
213.         UseFoundrySafety ? "Safety" : UseRealJudge ? "Judge" : "Stub";

215.     // Per-run timestamp ONLY for the report output folder under

217.     // ReportingConfiguration — that would scope the response cache per
218.     // run and defeat caching. Override with EVAL_REPORT_FOLDER in CI to
219.     // align with a build number.

221.         Environment.GetEnvironmentVariable("EVAL_REPORT_FOLDER")
222.             ?? DateTime.UtcNow.ToString("yyyyMMdd-HHmmss");
223. }

226. ## `golden.json` schema (v2)
227. 
228. ```json
229. {
230.   "schema_version": 2,
231.   "scenarios": [
232.     {
233.       "id": "g-receptionist-greeting",
234.       "user_message": "Hi, I'd like to start an interview.",
235.       "reference_response": "Hello! I'd be happy to start an interview with you. What role are you preparing for?",
236.       "context": null,
237.       "expected_traits": ["on_topic", "safe", "format_correct"],
238.       "expected_tool_calls": null
239.     }
240.   ]
241. }
242. ```
243. 
244. - `reference_response`: required for BLEU/GLEU/F1/Equivalence/Completeness.
245. - `context`: required for Groundedness. Free text providing the
246.   source-of-truth context the response should be grounded in.

248.   view. Read by the LLM judge.
249. - `expected_tool_calls`: required for `ToolCallAccuracyEvaluator`.
250. 
251. Migration from v1 (no `schema_version`, no `reference_response`): the
252. skill adds the fields as `null` so existing tests don't fail. NLP
253. evaluators emit `(no reference)` when null.

2. 
3. Compare mode runs the quality + telemetry pipeline against **multiple
4. model assignments** and produces a side-by-side report. Crucially, it
5. goes through the **same `DiskBasedReportingConfiguration`** so
6. `aieval report` aggregates the comparison into a single HTML view.

9. 
10. ```json
11. {
12.   "schema_version": 2,
13.   "entries": [
14.     {
15.       "name": "baseline-all-mini",
16.       "model_assignments": {
17.         "receptionist": "gpt-4o-mini",
18.         "behavioural":  "gpt-4o-mini",
19.         "technical":    "gpt-4o-mini",
20.         "summariser":   "gpt-4o-mini"
21.       }
22.     },
23.     {
24.       "name": "interviewers-upgraded",
25.       "model_assignments": {
26.         "receptionist": "gpt-4o-mini",
27.         "behavioural":  "gpt-4o",
28.         "technical":    "gpt-4o",
29.         "summariser":   "gpt-4o-mini"
30.       }
31.     }
32.   ]
33. }
34. ```

39. uses a **distinct `executionName`** so `aieval report` shows the
40. comparison side-by-side.

42. ```csharp
43. [TestClass]
44. public sealed class CompareTests
45. {
46.     public static IEnumerable<object[]> Matrix() =>
47.         MatrixLoader.Load().Select(e => new object[] { e });

49.     [TestMethod, DynamicData(nameof(Matrix), DynamicDataSourceType.Method)]
50.     public async Task RunEntry(MatrixEntry entry)
51.     {

53.         var reporting = DiskBasedReportingConfiguration.Create(

56.             chatConfiguration: new ChatConfiguration(

76. extension point. The generated factory (`AgentChatClientFactory`)
77. exposes an overload accepting per-agent model assignments — useful when
78. the app uses multiple deployment aliases or supports model swapping
79. via `ChatOptions.ModelId`.

102.         return root?.Entries ?? new();
103.     }

107. internal sealed record MatrixEntry(string Name, Dictionary<string, string> ModelAssignments);

111. `GoldenLoader.Load()` — STJ defaults will silently null-out PascalCase
112. properties bound to snake_case JSON.

115. 
116. `compare.md` (still emitted, in addition to the aggregated
117. `report.html`):
118. 
119. | name | avg ms | in tok | out tok | $ | mean quality | mean BLEU |
120. |------|--------|--------|---------|---|--------------|-----------|
121. | baseline-all-mini | 432 | 380 | 210 | 0.0021 | 3.8 | 0.31 |
122. | interviewers-upgraded | 891 | 380 | 245 | 0.0210 | 4.4 | 0.42 |
123. 
124. | Recommendation |
125. |----------------|
126. | `interviewers-upgraded`: +0.6 quality at +9.4× cost. Promote only if quality bar requires it. |
127. 
128. The recommendation row is rule-based:
129. 
130. - If cost increases > 3× and quality delta < 0.3 → **do not promote**.
131. - If cost increases ≤ 1.5× and quality delta ≥ 0.5 → **promote**.
132. - Otherwise → **manual review**.

1. # Evaluators catalog
2. 
3. Full catalog of evaluators wired by `setup-maf-evals`, grouped by tier.
4. The skill defaults to Tier 1 (NLP) always on, Tier 2 (Quality) on but
5. gated by `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE`, Tier 3 (Safety) off unless opted in.
6. 
7. Source: [learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/ai/evaluation/libraries](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/ai/evaluation/libraries)
8. 
9. ## Tier 1 — NLP (deterministic, no LLM)
10. 
11. Package: `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.NLP` (preview 10.7.0).
12. 
13. | Evaluator | Metric | Context type needed | Notes |
14. |-----------|--------|---------------------|-------|
15. | `BLEUEvaluator` | `BLEU` | `BLEUEvaluatorContext(IEnumerable<string> references)` | n-gram overlap with one or more reference strings |
16. | `GLEUEvaluator` | `GLEU` | `GLEUEvaluatorContext(IEnumerable<string> references)` | sentence-level BLEU variant |
17. | `F1Evaluator` | `F1` | `F1EvaluatorContext(string groundTruth)` | unigram-level F1 |
18. 
19. Plus a built-in custom evaluator the skill always scaffolds:
20. 
21. | Evaluator | Metric | Why |
22. |-----------|--------|-----|
23. | `WordCountEvaluator` (custom) | `Words` | Sanity check: response is non-empty and reasonable length. Same pattern as the Learn doc tutorial. |
24. 
25. ### `WordCountEvaluator` reference implementation
26. 
27. Scaffold this file verbatim (the Learn-doc canonical pattern) into
28. `Reporting/WordCountEvaluator.cs`. It runs in stub tier with no API key.
29. 
30. ```csharp
31. public sealed class WordCountEvaluator : IEvaluator
32. {
33.     public const string MetricName = "Words";
34.     public IReadOnlyCollection<string> EvaluationMetricNames { get; } = [MetricName];
35. 
36.     public ValueTask<EvaluationResult> EvaluateAsync(
37.         IEnumerable<ChatMessage> messages,
38.         ChatResponse modelResponse,
39.         ChatConfiguration? chatConfiguration = null,
40.         IEnumerable<EvaluationContext>? additionalContext = null,
41.         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
42.     {
43.         var text = modelResponse?.Text ?? string.Empty;
44.         var count = text.Split(
45.             new[] { ' ', '\t', '\r', '\n' },
46.             StringSplitOptions.RemoveEmptyEntries).Length;
47. 
48.         var metric = new NumericMetric(MetricName, value: count)
49.         {
50.             Interpretation = count switch
51.             {
52.                 < 5   => new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(EvaluationRating.Poor,    reason: "Response too short"),
53.                 > 500 => new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(EvaluationRating.Average, reason: "Response very long"),
54.                 _     => new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(EvaluationRating.Good),
55.             }
56.         };
57.         return new ValueTask<EvaluationResult>(new EvaluationResult(metric));
58.     }
59. }
60. ```
61. 
62. ## Tier 2 — Quality (LLM-as-judge)
63. 
64. Package: `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.Quality` (GA 10.7.0).
65. 
66. Requires `EVAL_USE_REAL_JUDGE=1` and a real `IChatClient`. The skill
67. wires the following by default:
68. 
69. | Evaluator | Metric | Context type | Notes |
70. |-----------|--------|--------------|-------|
71. | `RelevanceEvaluator` | `Relevance` | none | how relevant is the response to the query |
72. | `CoherenceEvaluator` | `Coherence` | none | logical, orderly presentation |
73. | `FluencyEvaluator` | `Fluency` | none | grammar, readability |
74. | `CompletenessEvaluator` | `Completeness` | `CompletenessEvaluatorContext(string groundTruth)` | comprehensive and accurate |
75. | `EquivalenceEvaluator` | `Equivalence` | `EquivalenceEvaluatorContext(string groundTruth)` | similarity vs ground truth wrt query |
76. | `GroundednessEvaluator` | `Groundedness` | `GroundednessEvaluatorContext(string context)` | alignment with given context |
77. 
78. Agent-focused (added when `*.AppHost.csproj` is detected, indicating
79. this is an agentic app and not just a chat completion app):
80. 
81. | Evaluator | Metric | Context type | Notes |
82. |-----------|--------|--------------|-------|
83. | `IntentResolutionEvaluator` | `Intent Resolution` | none | identifies + resolves user intent |
84. | `TaskAdherenceEvaluator` | `Task Adherence` | none | sticks to assigned task |
85. | `ToolCallAccuracyEvaluator` | `Tool Call Accuracy` | `ToolCallAccuracyEvaluatorContext(...)` | uses tools correctly |
86. 
87. **Not wired by default:** `RelevanceTruthAndCompletenessEvaluator`
88. (marked experimental in upstream docs), `RetrievalEvaluator` (specific
89. to RAG pipelines — separate skill territory).
90. 
91. ## Tier 3 — Safety (Foundry Evaluation service)
92. 
93. Package: `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.Safety` (preview 10.7.0).
94. 
95. Off by default. Enabled when user opts in during step 2 of the
96. workflow. Requires `EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY=1` and an Azure AI Foundry
97. endpoint (the skill prompts for `AZURE_AI_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT` + Entra credentials).
98. 
99. **Always wire the bundle, not the 4 separate evaluators:**
100. 
101. | Evaluator | Metrics produced | Notes |
102. |-----------|------------------|-------|
103. | `ContentHarmEvaluator` | `Hate And Unfairness`, `Self Harm`, `Violence`, `Sexual` | **Single-shot — one Foundry call returns all 4 metrics.** Always prefer this over the 4 separate evaluators below. |
104. 
105. Additional safety evaluators (each wired as separate `[TestMethod]`):
106. 
107. | Evaluator | Metric | Notes |
108. |-----------|--------|-------|
109. | `ProtectedMaterialEvaluator` | `Protected Material` | copyrighted material in output |
110. | `IndirectAttackEvaluator` | `Indirect Attack` | prompt-injection-style indirect attacks |
111. | `CodeVulnerabilityEvaluator` | `Code Vulnerability` | vulnerable code in output |
112. | `UngroundedAttributesEvaluator` | `Ungrounded Attributes` | inferred human attributes |
113. | `GroundednessProEvaluator` | `Groundedness Pro` | fine-tuned Foundry-hosted groundedness check |
114. 
115. The 4 separate evaluators (`HateAndUnfairnessEvaluator`,
116. `SelfHarmEvaluator`, `ViolenceEvaluator`, `SexualEvaluator`) are
117. **not** scaffolded — they're a strict subset of `ContentHarmEvaluator`
118. and cost 4× more Foundry calls for the same metrics.
119. 
120. ## Threshold mapping
121. 
122. `quality.thresholds.json` maps **real MEAI metric names** to minimum
123. `EvaluationRating` enum values:
124. 
125. ```json
126. {
127.   "schema_version": 2,
128.   "hard_fail": false,
129.   "thresholds": {
130.     "Relevance":   { "min_rating": "Good" },
131.     "Coherence":   { "min_rating": "Good" },
132.     "Fluency":     { "min_rating": "Average" },
133.     "Groundedness":{ "min_rating": "Good" },
134.     "BLEU":        { "min_value": 0.20 },
135.     "F1":          { "min_value": 0.30 },
136.     "Words":       { "min_value": 5, "max_value": 500 }
137.   }
138. }
139. ```
140. 
141. `hard_fail: true` makes any below-threshold metric fail the test.
142. Default `false` makes the test pass-through informational — failures
143. show in the report only.
144. 
145. ## Custom rubric-driven evaluator
146. 
147. The built-in Quality evaluators (Relevance, Coherence, Fluency,
148. Completeness, Equivalence) judge against generic rubrics baked into
149. the evaluator's judge prompt. They cannot read `Quality/rubric.md`.
150. That makes them ill-fitting for agents with deliberate stylistic
151. constraints (ELI5 / summarizer / strict-format / persona-bound
152. agents) — see `common-pitfalls.md#tuning-quality-for-stylistic-agents`.
153. 
154. For those agents, scaffold a `RubricEvaluator` that reads
155. `Quality/rubric.md` and asks the judge to score against *your*
156. criteria. The pattern is shape-identical to `WordCountEvaluator` —
157. it just delegates to the judge chat client.
158. 
159. ```csharp
160. // Reporting/RubricEvaluator.cs
161. // Custom rubric-driven evaluator. Reads Quality/rubric.md and asks
162. // the judge to score the response against per-app criteria. Emits a
163. // single "RubricFit" metric (numeric 1-5) plus a free-text rationale.
164. public sealed class RubricEvaluator : IEvaluator
165. {
166.     public const string MetricName = "RubricFit";
167.     public IReadOnlyCollection<string> EvaluationMetricNames { get; } = [MetricName];
168. 
169.     private readonly string _rubric;
170. 
171.     public RubricEvaluator(string rubricMarkdown) => _rubric = rubricMarkdown;
172. 
173.     public static RubricEvaluator FromFile(string path) =>
174.         new(File.ReadAllText(path));
175. 
176.     public async ValueTask<EvaluationResult> EvaluateAsync(
177.         IEnumerable<ChatMessage> messages,
178.         ChatResponse modelResponse,
179.         ChatConfiguration? chatConfiguration = null,
180.         IEnumerable<EvaluationContext>? additionalContext = null,
181.         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
182.     {
183.         if (chatConfiguration?.ChatClient is null)
184.         {
185.             // Judge tier not active — return a stubbed Inconclusive metric.
186.             return new EvaluationResult(new NumericMetric(MetricName)
187.             {
188.                 Interpretation = new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(
189.                     EvaluationRating.Inconclusive, reason: "Judge not wired.")
190.             });
191.         }
192. 
193.         var userQuery = string.Join("\n", messages.Select(m => m.Text));
194.         var responseText = modelResponse.Text ?? string.Empty;
195. 
196.         // NOTE: $$"""...""" (double-$) raw string. Inside, single { } is literal
197.         // (matters for the JSON braces below), and {{var}} is interpolation.
198.         // Plain $"""...""" would reject `{{ ... }}` as literal with CS9006.
199.         var prompt = $$"""
200.             You are scoring an assistant response against the rubric below.
201. 
202.             ## Rubric
203.             {{_rubric}}
204. 
205.             ## User query
206.             {{userQuery}}
207. 
208.             ## Assistant response
209.             {{responseText}}
210. 
211.             Respond with strict JSON: { "score": <1-5 int>, "rationale": "<1-2 sentences>" }.
212.             5 = perfectly satisfies every rubric clause. 1 = ignores the rubric.
213.             """;
214. 
215.         var judge = await chatConfiguration.ChatClient.GetResponseAsync(
216.             prompt, cancellationToken: cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
217. 
218.         // Tolerant parse: fall back to Inconclusive on bad JSON.
219.         var (score, rationale) = TryParse(judge.Text ?? "");
220. 
221.         var metric = new NumericMetric(MetricName, value: score)
222.         {
223.             Interpretation = new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(
224.                 rating: score switch { >= 4 => EvaluationRating.Good,
225.                                        3    => EvaluationRating.Average,
226.                                        _    => EvaluationRating.Poor },
227.                 reason: rationale)
228.         };
229.         return new EvaluationResult(metric);
230.     }
231. 
232.     private static (int score, string rationale) TryParse(string raw)
233.     {
234.         try
235.         {
236.             using var doc = JsonDocument.Parse(raw.Trim().Trim('`', ' ', '\n', '\r'));
237.             return (doc.RootElement.GetProperty("score").GetInt32(),
238.                     doc.RootElement.GetProperty("rationale").GetString() ?? "");
239.         }
240.         catch { return (3, "Judge response was unparseable; defaulted to Average."); }
241.     }
242. }
243. ```
244. 
245. Wire it from `Reporting/ReportingConfig.cs`'s judge-tier evaluator
246. list **alongside** Relevance/Coherence/Fluency (drop Completeness +
247. Equivalence per the pitfall guidance):
248. 
249. ```csharp
250. // In ReportingConfig.ForQuality(), when EvalEnv.UseRealJudge:
251. evaluators.Add(new RelevanceEvaluator());
252. evaluators.Add(new CoherenceEvaluator());
253. evaluators.Add(new FluencyEvaluator());
254. evaluators.Add(RubricEvaluator.FromFile(
255.     Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Quality", "rubric.md")));
256. // CompletenessEvaluator + EquivalenceEvaluator deliberately dropped
257. // for this app — see common-pitfalls.md tuning section.
258. ```
259. 
260. Ensure `Quality/rubric.md` is copied to output by adding to the csproj:
261. 
262. ```xml
263. <ItemGroup>
264.   <None Update="Quality/rubric.md" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
265. </ItemGroup>
266. ```
267. 
268. This `RubricFit` metric will appear in `report.html` alongside the
269. built-ins, and the rationale shows in the per-scenario detail drawer.
270. Update `Reporting/MetricsGlossary.cs`'s `QualityEntries` constant to
271. add a one-line `RubricFit` definition pointing at `Quality/rubric.md`.
272.

76. | `GroundednessEvaluator` | `Groundedness` | `GroundednessEvaluatorContext(string context)` | alignment with given context |
77. 
78. Agent-focused (added when `*.AppHost.csproj` is detected, indicating
79. this is an agentic app and not just a chat completion app):
80. 
81. | Evaluator | Metric | Context type | Notes |
82. |-----------|--------|--------------|-------|
83. | `IntentResolutionEvaluator` | `Intent Resolution` | none | identifies + resolves user intent |
84. | `TaskAdherenceEvaluator` | `Task Adherence` | none | sticks to assigned task |
85. | `ToolCallAccuracyEvaluator` | `Tool Call Accuracy` | `ToolCallAccuracyEvaluatorContext(...)` | uses tools correctly |
86. 
87. **Not wired by default:** `RelevanceTruthAndCompletenessEvaluator`
88. (marked experimental in upstream docs), `RetrievalEvaluator` (specific
89. to RAG pipelines — separate skill territory).
90. 
91. ## Tier 3 — Safety (Foundry Evaluation service)
92. 
93. Package: `Microsoft.Extensions.AI.Evaluation.Safety` (preview 10.7.0).
94. 
95. Off by default. Enabled when user opts in during step 2 of the
96. workflow. Requires `EVAL_USE_FOUNDRY_SAFETY=1` and an Azure AI Foundry
97. endpoint (the skill prompts for `AZURE_AI_FOUNDRY_ENDPOINT` + Entra credentials).
98. 
99. **Always wire the bundle, not the 4 separate evaluators:**
100. 
101. | Evaluator | Metrics produced | Notes |
102. |-----------|------------------|-------|
103. | `ContentHarmEvaluator` | `Hate And Unfairness`, `Self Harm`, `Violence`, `Sexual` | **Single-shot — one Foundry call returns all 4 metrics.** Always prefer this over the 4 separate evaluators below. |
104. 
105. Additional safety evaluators (each wired as separate `[TestMethod]`):
106. 
107. | Evaluator | Metric | Notes |
108. |-----------|--------|-------|
109. | `ProtectedMaterialEvaluator` | `Protected Material` | copyrighted material in output |
110. | `IndirectAttackEvaluator` | `Indirect Attack` | prompt-injection-style indirect attacks |
111. | `CodeVulnerabilityEvaluator` | `Code Vulnerability` | vulnerable code in output |
112. | `UngroundedAttributesEvaluator` | `Ungrounded Attributes` | inferred human attributes |
113. | `GroundednessProEvaluator` | `Groundedness Pro` | fine-tuned Foundry-hosted groundedness check |
114. 
115. The 4 separate evaluators (`HateAndUnfairnessEvaluator`,
116. `SelfHarmEvaluator`, `ViolenceEvaluator`, `SexualEvaluator`) are
117. **not** scaffolded — they're a strict subset of `ContentHarmEvaluator`
118. and cost 4× more Foundry calls for the same metrics.
119. 
120. ## Threshold mapping
121. 
122. `quality.thresholds.json` maps **real MEAI metric names** to minimum
123. `EvaluationRating` enum values:
124. 
125. ```json
126. {
127.   "schema_version": 2,
128.   "hard_fail": false,
129.   "thresholds": {
130.     "Relevance":   { "min_rating": "Good" },
131.     "Coherence":   { "min_rating": "Good" },
132.     "Fluency":     { "min_rating": "Average" },
133.     "Groundedness":{ "min_rating": "Good" },
134.     "BLEU":        { "min_value": 0.20 },
135.     "F1":          { "min_value": 0.30 },
136.     "Words":       { "min_value": 5, "max_value": 500 }
137.   }
138. }
139. ```
140. 
141. `hard_fail: true` makes any below-threshold metric fail the test.
142. Default `false` makes the test pass-through informational — failures
143. show in the report only.
144. 
145. ## Custom rubric-driven evaluator
146. 
147. The built-in Quality evaluators (Relevance, Coherence, Fluency,
148. Completeness, Equivalence) judge against generic rubrics baked into
149. the evaluator's judge prompt. They cannot read `Quality/rubric.md`.
150. That makes them ill-fitting for agents with deliberate stylistic
151. constraints (ELI5 / summarizer / strict-format / persona-bound
152. agents) — see `common-pitfalls.md#tuning-quality-for-stylistic-agents`.
153. 
154. For those agents, scaffold a `RubricEvaluator` that reads
155. `Quality/rubric.md` and asks the judge to score against *your*
156. criteria. The pattern is shape-identical to `WordCountEvaluator` —
157. it just delegates to the judge chat client.
158. 
159. ```csharp
160. // Reporting/RubricEvaluator.cs
161. // Custom rubric-driven evaluator. Reads Quality/rubric.md and asks
162. // the judge to score the response against per-app criteria. Emits a
163. // single "RubricFit" metric (numeric 1-5) plus a free-text rationale.
164. public sealed class RubricEvaluator : IEvaluator
165. {
166.     public const string MetricName = "RubricFit";
167.     public IReadOnlyCollection<string> EvaluationMetricNames { get; } = [MetricName];
168. 
169.     private readonly string _rubric;
170. 
171.     public RubricEvaluator(string rubricMarkdown) => _rubric = rubricMarkdown;
172. 
173.     public static RubricEvaluator FromFile(string path) =>
174.         new(File.ReadAllText(path));
175. 
176.     public async ValueTask<EvaluationResult> EvaluateAsync(
177.         IEnumerable<ChatMessage> messages,
178.         ChatResponse modelResponse,
179.         ChatConfiguration? chatConfiguration = null,
180.         IEnumerable<EvaluationContext>? additionalContext = null,
181.         CancellationToken cancellationToken = default)
182.     {
183.         if (chatConfiguration?.ChatClient is null)
184.         {
185.             // Judge tier not active — return a stubbed Inconclusive metric.
186.             return new EvaluationResult(new NumericMetric(MetricName)
187.             {
188.                 Interpretation = new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(
189.                     EvaluationRating.Inconclusive, reason: "Judge not wired.")
190.             });
191.         }
192. 
193.         var userQuery = string.Join("\n", messages.Select(m => m.Text));
194.         var responseText = modelResponse.Text ?? string.Empty;
195. 
196.         // NOTE: $$"""...""" (double-$) raw string. Inside, single { } is literal
197.         // (matters for the JSON braces below), and {{var}} is interpolation.
198.         // Plain $"""...""" would reject `{{ ... }}` as literal with CS9006.
199.         var prompt = $$"""
200.             You are scoring an assistant response against the rubric below.
201. 
202.             ## Rubric
203.             {{_rubric}}
204. 
205.             ## User query
206.             {{userQuery}}
207. 
208.             ## Assistant response
209.             {{responseText}}
210. 
211.             Respond with strict JSON: { "score": <1-5 int>, "rationale": "<1-2 sentences>" }.
212.             5 = perfectly satisfies every rubric clause. 1 = ignores the rubric.
213.             """;
214. 
215.         var judge = await chatConfiguration.ChatClient.GetResponseAsync(
216.             prompt, cancellationToken: cancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
217. 
218.         // Tolerant parse: fall back to Inconclusive on bad JSON.
219.         var (score, rationale) = TryParse(judge.Text ?? "");
220. 
221.         var metric = new NumericMetric(MetricName, value: score)
222.         {
223.             Interpretation = new EvaluationMetricInterpretation(
224.                 rating: score switch { >= 4 => EvaluationRating.Good,
225.                                        3    => EvaluationRating.Average,
226.                                        _    => EvaluationRating.Poor },
227.                 reason: rationale)
228.         };
229.         return new EvaluationResult(metric);
230.     }
231. 
232.     private static (int score, string rationale) TryParse(string raw)
233.     {
234.         try
235.         {
236.             using var doc = JsonDocument.Parse(raw.Trim().Trim('`', ' ', '\n', '\r'));
237.             return (doc.RootElement.GetProperty("score").GetInt32(),
238.                     doc.RootElement.GetProperty("rationale").GetString() ?? "");
239.         }
240.         catch { return (3, "Judge response was unparseable; defaulted to Average."); }
241.     }
242. }
243. ```
244. 
245. Wire it from `Reporting/ReportingConfig.cs`'s judge-tier evaluator
246. list **alongside** Relevance/Coherence/Fluency (drop Completeness +
247. Equivalence per the pitfall guidance):
248. 
249. ```csharp
250. // In ReportingConfig.ForQuality(), when EvalEnv.UseRealJudge:
251. evaluators.Add(new RelevanceEvaluator());
252. evaluators.Add(new CoherenceEvaluator());
253. evaluators.Add(new FluencyEvaluator());
254. evaluators.Add(RubricEvaluator.FromFile(
255.     Path.Combine(AppContext.BaseDirectory, "Quality", "rubric.md")));
256. // CompletenessEvaluator + EquivalenceEvaluator deliberately dropped
257. // for this app — see common-pitfalls.md tuning section.
258. ```
259. 
260. Ensure `Quality/rubric.md` is copied to output by adding to the csproj:
261. 
262. ```xml
263. <ItemGroup>
264.   <None Update="Quality/rubric.md" CopyToOutputDirectory="PreserveNewest" />
265. </ItemGroup>
266. ```
267. 
268. This `RubricFit` metric will appear in `report.html` alongside the
269. built-ins, and the rationale shows in the per-scenario detail drawer.
270. Update `Reporting/MetricsGlossary.cs`'s `QualityEntries` constant to
271. add a one-line `RubricFit` definition pointing at `Quality/rubric.md`.
